Wisconsin's known data center footprint covers six facilities, concentrated around Milwaukee, with no capacity figures recorded, making it impossible to assess the state's actual power draw or AI-hosting potential from this data alone.

Four of the six sites cluster within the greater Milwaukee metro area, including Franklin and Waukesha. The remaining two sit further west, in Dane County and Marquette County. That geographic spread suggests the inventory is not simply a Milwaukee list, but the density near the city still dominates.

One facility is operated by a regional telephone cooperative, one by a utility, WE Energies, and three by named colocation providers. The utility-operated site is notable because it places power infrastructure and data center operations under the same entity, a structural relationship that can simplify capacity negotiation. What this data does not provide is megawatt figures for any facility, so no inference about grid load, available power headroom, or AI workload suitability is possible here.
